sentences: `vk_pipeline_check <spirv dir> pipeline_cache.bin --jobs 4` on an RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA 595 driver): **all 26,503 shaders become real pipelines, 0 failures** (cs 2,689, ps 12,101, ms 9,282, vs 2,236, gs 195; graphics stages with generated stub partners).
Compile time 40,784 s of CPU (2.84 h wall on 4 threads): cs 23,633 s (mean 8.8 s; the ray-tracing ScreenProbes/RTShadowTrace shaders take 2-19 min each), ps 11,481 s, ms 5,395 s, vs 275 s.
The resulting `VkPipelineCache` is 3.81 GB; seeding a run with it makes those pipelines instant, which is what a fast first boot needs.
The cache is per driver and GPU, and a shader whose SPIR-V changes compiles again (the checker resumes from the file).

Neither register storage (one variable per register) nor smaller SPIR-V cut NVIDIA compile time: the big ray-tracing shaders are expensive as such, so the runtime should compile them in the background rather than block on them.
